newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends weaker, drawn lower by weak crude.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends weaker, drawn lower by weak crude.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended weaker drawn lower with crude after putting on $3.50 a tonne in early business on the back of tight Rotterdam supply, traders said.
Brent futures fell over half a dollar in active selling following news the U.N. and Iraq had agreed on aid plan details and on German plans to sell crude oil.
The August gas oil contract last traded $1.50 down at $160.50 a tonne after falling from a high of $165.25 built on talk of tight Rotterdam supplies and delayed barge loadings.
Physical trade was thin though with a strong dollar versus the mark keeping demand from the key German market quiet though inland refiners reported good business.

"The Germans are buying cheaper oil inland" one broker said. A backlog of barges waiting to load at the jointly owned BP, Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam was also seen causing short-term supply problems, traders said.
"The problem is that everybody wants to load on the 16th and in order to avoid demurrage costs the refiners have put some nominations for the 16th back to the 18th," one trader said.
August Brent was trading 16 cents a barrel lower at $17.93 after holding support at $17.80 following a fall from an $18.45 high on the Iraq German oil sales news.

It was not immediately clear when the Iraqi oil sales would resume but there was talk that the whole process may be concluded by next Monday, including the official submission by the government of Iraq to the secretary-general of the United Nations.

Confirmation by the German economics ministry that it would sell 2.8 million barrels of crude oil from strategic crude oil reserves in its first tender starting August 4 was also seen as bearish by the market.
